text:
alex: perf-bot flagged a CI perf failure on PR 12567. bench_batcher_prefetch_latency exceeded threshold by 12% (median).
perf-bot: CI perf diff detected: bench_batcher_prefetch_latency: +12.1% (threshold +5%), kv_hit_rate: -8.3%.
maya.dev: Ugh — this was a large merge that touched kernel selection + prefetch heuristics. Repro locally with `./scripts/ci_perf --bench=batcher_prefetch --runs=10` and I can see latency regressed.
sophie: Can you paste the CI diff? link?
alex: https://perf.redwood.local/dash/12567 (CI graphs). Key point: median p50 increased from 18.3ms -> 20.6ms, p95 72ms -> 95ms. KV hit-rate drop correlates with prefetch misses.
li: I ran `git bisect` across the last 6 merges. Suspect commit 8f3b2d0 (adaptive-prefetch: lower prefetch ms for tiny batches).
jonathan: That commit changed batch_prefetch_ms default from 5 -> 2 and added kernel_score weighting. Could cause more small-batch fast-paths that miss cached KV.
maya.dev: Reproduced with the microbench harness. Logs:
```
bench: batcher_prefetch_latency
config: batch_prefetch_ms=2
median: 20.7ms
kv_hit_rate: 91.2%
```
Then with previous config:
```
batch_prefetch_ms=5
median: 18.4ms
kv_hit_rate: 99.6%
```
perf-bot: perf unit test failing: test_batcher_prefetch_threshold (expected <= +5% got +12.1%).
alex: Suggest hotfix: revert the default to 5ms on CI only or pin kernel selection to previous heuristics for canary.
sophie: Agree. Also add a microbench that simulates mixed-seqlen workload to catch this earlier.
li: I can open a revert PR for the default change and add a regression test. Anyone object?
jonathan: +1. Also log an issue to revisit kernel_score weighting — it may be over-optimizing for throughput at cost of cache locality.
maya.dev: I'll attach traces and a perf flame for the failing run in the PR. For now, marking this a rollout blocker.
ci-bot: Deploy-blocker: PR 12567 flagged for perf regression. Auto-block enabled.
alex: Thanks — working on revert PR now, will link once ready. :thumbsup:
